action: Poste Italiane customers: be wary of emails, calls or texts that use your name, contact details or contract information; do not share credentials.
date_note: Date of the forum post the article describes; Cybersecurity360 published November 19.
exec: Customer contracts and contact details tied to a digital-signature service were reportedly leaked, raising phishing and fraud risk for customers of a major Italian provider.
plain: Poste Italiane told an Italian news site it had a data breach affecting a limited number of people, reported as over 1,500 customers. Names, emails and contract documents were reportedly exposed; Poste says payment credentials are safe.
summary: Cybersecurity360 reports that Poste Italiane confirmed a breach affecting a limited number of people, reported as over 1,500 customers, with checks still under way. Files of about 1 GB, linked to the PosteCert remote digital-signature service, include names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and contract documents. Poste says passwords and payment credentials are safe. The cause is not stated.
title: Poste Italiane confirms data breach, over 1,500 customers exposed

validation.note: One outlet (Cybersecurity360, Nov 19) read in full; it quotes Poste's own comment. A forum user's claim of the leak is unverified and not used as attribution.
